ideas.pitch: A real-time worker safety compliance system running computer vision locally on a Raspberry Pi with a connected camera to detect missing hardhats and vests without sending video streams to the cloud.
ideas.title: EdgeGuard Industrial Safety Monitor
ideas.why_it_could_win: Directly targets the image and signal processing domain and industrial safety requirements while demonstrating a live on-site hardware demo, following the pattern of the hackathon-winning industrial safety detection system.

ideas.pitch: An automated waste segregation prototype utilizing an ESP32 microcontroller, a TCS3200 color sensor, and a servo-driven trapdoor to sort dry and wet waste at the point of disposal.
ideas.title: EcoSort Smart Bin
ideas.why_it_could_win: Aligns with the ESP32/Arduino track and features a physical, interactive hardware prototype that guarantees a reliable live demonstration for judges.

ideas.pitch: A wearable biomedical monitoring prototype built on an ESP32 that measures heart rate and SpO2 via a MAX30102 sensor, performing local threshold anomaly detection and triggering local buzzer alarms during critical drops.
ideas.title: PulseGuard Edge Telemetry Unit
ideas.why_it_could_win: Matches the Biomedical Engineering problem domain and showcases real-time edge computing for patient telemetry, mirroring winning embedded healthcare concepts.

ideas.pitch: A hardware-implemented finite impulse response (FIR) filter on an FPGA development board to clean up noisy real-time analog signals from environmental sensors instantly.
ideas.title: FPGA-Accelerated FIR Filter for Sensor Noise
ideas.why_it_could_win: Targets the FPGA track and the Processor Design / Image and Signal Processing problem domains by showcasing low-level, high-performance hardware description language implementation.

ideas.pitch: An ESP32-based logistics tracker featuring a conductive ink continuity loop that detects physical seal breakage and immediately alerts local wireless receivers.
ideas.title: ChainVerify Tamper-Evident Cargo Tag
ideas.why_it_could_win: Addresses Defence and Security problem domains using cheap edge microcontrollers to detect physical tampering, following the prize-winning anti-counterfeiting hardware logistics pattern.
